title: Missed Installments and the Raise on an Add-On Down Payment
content:
**Revenue Cycle Policy Manual — Patient Payment Plans: raise of the add-on down payment for missed installments**

**Clause.** How missed installments raise the add-on down payment depends on how the plan's installments are drawn and on its payment record: for a plan drawn automatically from a bank account with at least 6 scheduled installments paid less than 12 whole months before today, only the latest missed installment raises it, by one quarter, however many were recorded in that span; for a plan drawn automatically from a credit or debit card with at least 6 scheduled installments paid in that span, every missed installment recorded in that span raises it by one quarter of the amount already raised, the raises compounding; for any other plan the raise is one quarter for one missed installment and one half for two or more.

**Records read.**
- *Missed installments in the span*: missed-installment lines on the plan ledger dated less than 12 whole months before today.
- *Scheduled installments paid in the span*: payments on the plan ledger posted as scheduled installments and dated less than 12 whole months before today.
- *How the plan is drawn*: the plan's automatic-payment setting and the method on file for automatic draws — bank transfer (ACH), or a credit or debit card.

## The three methods

| Plan | Missed installments in the span | Raise multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| Automatic draws from a bank account, at least 6 scheduled installments paid in the span | none | none (1) |
| — same — | 1 or more, however many | 1.25 (one quarter) |
| Automatic draws from a credit or debit card, at least 6 scheduled installments paid in the span | none | none (1) |
| — same — | *n* | the product of *n* factors of 1.25: 1.25 for one, 1.5625 for two, 1.953125 for three |
| Any other plan (manual payment, or fewer than 6 scheduled installments paid in the span) | none | none (1) |
| — same — | exactly 1 | 1.25 (one quarter) |
| — same — | 2 or more | 1.5 (one half) |

The compounding method raises the amount by one quarter for the first missed installment, then raises that raised amount by a further quarter for the second, and so on; the result is rounded to the nearest cent only once, at the end, an exact half cent being rounded up.

## Hypothetical illustrations (amount before any raise: 40.00; 3 missed installments in the span)

| Plan | Multiplier | Raised amount |
|---|---|---|
| Bank-transfer draws, 8 scheduled installments paid in the span | 1.25 | 50.00 |
| Debit-card draws, 8 scheduled installments paid in the span | 1.953125 | 78.13 (78.125 rounded up at the half cent) |
| Debit-card draws, 5 scheduled installments paid in the span | 1.5 | 60.00 |
| Paid manually, 10 scheduled installments paid in the span | 1.5 | 60.00 |
